raw_response:
I will still farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little for price, water, and labor. I have 12 mu, and with wheat-maize being my main pattern, I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around here, if I cut fertilizer too hard and the stand turns weak, I cannot get that yield back, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the field go hungry. But I do not throw money blindly either. I have middle school education, so I do look at soil condition, crop color, and whether the land has enough base fertilizer, not just copy one fixed number every year. Still, I watch what farmers nearby do. If the neighbors get a good wheat head and good maize ear with a certain rate, I stay close to that. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water to support the fertilizer, especially for wheat and maize. Family labor is not as full as before because some people work outside, so I will keep the plan steady and not make it too complicated. This year I will put 10 mu into wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu into cotton. Wheat is the backbone for grain, maize gives me steady summer output, and cotton I will keep on a small area because it needs more watching and more spraying.
